column1: # recursion-closure-policy.tsv — THE RECURSION FIREWALL, AS DATA.
# Enforced by `scripts/check-recursion-closure.py` against `cargo metadata`'s
# resolve, over NORMAL + BUILD edges (the library graph — what a consumer links).
# `dev` edges are excluded; see that script's docstring for why that is not a
# loophole and why the green control is itself the proof of it.
# Tab-separated.  Row kinds:
#   MARK      <pkg>                  <reason>
#       A package that IS the recursion fork.  The `@recursion` group expands to
#       every MARK row, so a NEW recursion crate is covered by every existing
#       FORBID row the moment it is marked here.
#   FORBID    <crate>  <target>      <reason>
#       No normal/build path from <crate> to <target>.  <target> may be `@recursion`.
#   REQUIRE   <crate>  <target>      <reason>
#       There IS such a path.  ⚑ These rows are why this gate cannot be satisfied
#       by deletion.  "nothing reaches the recursion fork" is trivially true of a
#       tree that can no longer verify anything.
#   REQUIRE_DIRECT  <crate>  <target>  <reason>
#       <crate> DECLARES <target> in its OWN manifest — one hop.  ⚑ Use this
#       wherever the claim is about a VISIBLE edge, which is most of them: the
#       first draft of this file wrote `REQUIRE dregg-node dregg-recursion-verify`
#       and the gate's own red-proof refused to go red when that edge was deleted,
#       because `dregg-node -> dregg-circuit-prove -> dregg-recursion-verify`
#       satisfies the REACH through a path the node does not own.  The row was
#       true and useless while reading as the capability check.
# ⚠ THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST OF WHO MAY TAKE THE EDGE.  123 of 227 workspace
# members legitimately reach the recursion fork (measured 2026-08-05) and a list
# of those would be a snapshot that rots weekly, not a rule.  The firewall is the
# set that must NOT — plus the small set that MUST.
MARK
column3: The recursion fork's circuit/AIR types (rev fc3c6df).

column1: MARK
column3: Carries BatchStarkProver::verify_all_tables — the actual recursive check, and the prover with it.

column1: MARK
column3: The heavy dregg prove surface: the IVC tower, the shielded prover, the custom proof-bind engine, the wgpu/pollster GPU backend.

column1: # ⚑ `dregg-turn` is THE claim this gate was written for.  turn/Cargo.toml:17-25
# has forbidden this edge in prose since the prover extraction, and nothing
# checked it; the comment's own two justifications (an seL4 verifier-PD floor
# that builds no dregg crate, a wasm card that declares circuit-prove on purpose)
# had both expired unnoticed.  What is still real is the cfg-brittleness argument
# in TURN-PROVER-CRATE-EXTRACTION-DESIGN.md §0 plus the weight the ~50 crates
# downstream of turn inherit.  The edge stays out; a consumer that WANTS recursion
# verification takes `dregg-recursion-verify` explicitly, and turn fails the
# effect CLOSED when no backend is injected.
FORBID
column4: Core turn is recursion-free. A consumer that wants root verification injects a MinaChainRootBackend (executor/mina_head_verifier.rs); turn REFUSES when none is.

column1: # The verify floor everything else stands on. If `dregg-circuit` ever took the
# edge, every FORBID row below would fall in the same commit and the wall would
# be gone in one move.
FORBID
column4: The verify-level descriptor/PI floor. Its whole value is being the light crate ~200 members can depend on.

column1: FORBID
column4: The cell/predicate substrate. A witnessed predicate is verified by an INJECTED verifier, never by linking a prover.

column1: FORBID
column4: Consensus. The quorum path verifies; it does not prove.

column1: FORBID
column4: The durable store. Nothing about writing a commit log needs the recursion fork.

column1: # ⚑ THE ROW THAT MAKES THE EXTRACTION REAL RATHER THAN COSMETIC.
# `dregg-recursion-verify` exists to be the SMALL edge: a consumer takes it to
# gain root VERIFICATION without the IVC tower, the shielded prover, the GPU
# backend, dregg-lean-ffi, dregg-cell, dregg-commit, dregg-p3-pasta or p3-bn254.
# It declares dregg-circuit-prove as a DEV-dependency (its seam test mints a real
# fold, then consumes the root through the verify path) and that is fine — a dev
# edge links into its own test binaries and nothing a consumer builds.  Promote
# that dev-dep into [dependencies] and every consumer silently inherits the whole
# tower while the crate's own tests behave identically.  This row is what notices.
FORBID
column4: The verify crate must stay the SMALL edge. Its circuit-prove dep is dev-only, on purpose.

column1: # ── the capability, asserted in the positive ─────────────────────────────────
# ⚑ Without these rows the gate is satisfiable by deleting the feature. A firewall
# check that only measures ABSENCE measures the cheap direction.
REQUIRE_DIRECT
column4: It must actually carry the FriRecursionConfig impl the orphan rule pins to the fork.

column1: REQUIRE_DIRECT
column4: verify_all_tables IS the recursive check. Without this edge the crate cannot verify a root at all.

column1: # ⚑ THE NODE'S CAPABILITY, AND ITS SILENCE IF LOST. `MinaAnchoredHeadStarkVerifier`
# is constructed UNWIRED and refuses every Mina anchored head at refusal 0. If the
# node's edge to the verify crate went away, the node would still build, still run,
# and silently stop being able to verify a head — the UN-CALLED INITIALIZER shape.
# DIRECT, because the whole operator rule is that the capability is a dependency you
# can SEE. Reaching the crate through circuit-prove is not the node taking the edge.
REQUIRE_DIRECT
column4: The node injects the P3MinaChainRootBackend. Lose this edge and the node refuses every Mina head, silently.

column1: # The config/fingerprint/verify entry points MOVED to the verify crate and are
# re-exported from plonky3_recursion_impl::recursive. A verify-side COPY would be
# the "two shapes that agree today" failure; this row says the move stayed a move.
REQUIRE_DIRECT
column4: The verify half was EXTRACTED, not copied. circuit-prove re-exports it.

column1: # The one row where the REACH is the point rather than the declaration: whatever the
# node's manifest says, the code that actually runs `verify_all_tables` must be in
# the node's link. This is the capability, stated at the closure level.
REQUIRE
column4: The node must LINK the recursive verifier itself, by whatever path.
